title: A Dual-Branch Graph and Convolutional Network for Interpretable Movement EEG Classification
abstract: arXiv:2611.16609v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Decoding upper-limb movements from scalp electroencephalography (EEG) is an important problem for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), but many deep learning models provide limited insight into the brain regions underlying their predictions. We propose a two-branch architecture that combines an LGGNet-inspired local-global graph branch with an EEGNet-style convolutional branch for movement-versus-rest classification. The graph branch groups 61 EEG electrodes into anatomically informed regions and learns their spatial relationships, providing a direct representation of the regions emphasized by the model. We evaluate the proposed architecture using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation on the Ofner upper-limb movement dataset. The model achieves a mean F1-score of 0.74 +/- 0.06 across subjects. translated_title: 一种用于可解释运动脑电（EEG）分类的双分支图与卷积网络
translated_abstract: 从头皮脑电图（EEG）中解码上肢运动是脑机接口（BCI）领域的一个重要问题，但许多深度学习模型对其预测所依赖的脑区域提供的洞察十分有限。我们提出了一种双分支架构，将受LGGNet启发的局部-全局图分支与EEGNet风格的卷积分支相结合，用于运动与静息状态的分类。图分支将61个EEG电极按照解剖学信息划分为若干脑区域，并学习这些区域之间的空间关系，从而直接呈现模型所重点关注的脑区域。我们在Ofner上肢运动数据集上采用留一被试交叉验证对该架构进行评估，模型在各被试上的平均F1分数达到0.74 ± 0.06。除了分类性能之外，我们还分析了学习到的图结构，以识别连接最强的脑区域。在所有留出的……
tldr: 该论文提出一种结合解剖学信息图分支与EEGNet卷积分支的双分支网络，在上肢运动脑电分类中取得良好性能的同时，可通过学习到的图结构直接揭示模型所依赖的关键脑区域，实现可解释性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a dual-branch network combining an anatomically informed graph branch with an EEGNet-style convolutional branch, achieving strong upper-limb movement EEG classification performance while providing interpretability into the brain regions underlying the model's predictions.
